claims.text: Introducing SRO precipitates into crystalline PbTe will reduce its lattice thermal conductivity.
SRO precipitates enhance phonon scattering in PbTe.
The initial PbTe is highly crystalline and largely defect-free.
The initial PbTe contains no pre-existing SRO precipitates.
Doping or thermal treatment can form controlled SRO precipitates within a PbTe matrix.
Electronic contributions can be minimized so that lattice thermal conductivity is isolated.
SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
Increased phonon scattering shortens the phonon mean free path.
A shorter phonon mean free path reduces the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity.
PbTe with induced SRO precipitates will have statistically significantly lower lattice thermal conductivity than SRO-free PbTe under identical test conditions.
A significant effect requires an optimal range of precipitate size, density, and distribution.
Precipitate concentrations outside the optimal range may produce negligible differences or competing phenomena.
Precipitate coarsening could mask the proposed phonon-scattering effect.
Direct evidence for the specific role of SRO precipitates in PbTe is currently lacking.
TEM or XRD can be used to verify the presence, size, and density of SRO precipitates.
Failure to observe a conductivity reduction beyond experimental uncertainty, or failure to find a correlation with precipitate characteristics, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline calls for the control and treated material to be measured under the same 'structural conditions,' although the hypothesis requires them to differ structurally through the presence or absence of SRO precipitates.
